title: Owner forms: minun, sinun, hänen, meidän, teidän, heidän
focus: Finnish uses an owner form called the genitive before a personal possessive noun. Learn the six owner forms from their basic pronouns.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Finnish owner form meaning “my”.
exercises.explanation: The owner form of minä is minun. This genitive pronoun tells whose thing it is.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Genitive personal owner forms: form or meaning confused

optionFeedback.minun: The owner form of minä is minun. This genitive pronoun tells whose thing it is.
optionFeedback.sinun: sinun means your for one person.
optionFeedback.teidän: teidän means your for a group.

answerDiagnostics.category: Genitive personal owner forms: predictable form error
answerDiagnostics.explanation: Use the genitive owner form, not the basic personal pronoun.
